title: Print did not standardise European vernaculars uniformly
body:
Re-reading Eisenstein and recent revisions (Pettegree 2010).
[Step] Source review
  [Input] Eisenstein 1979, Pettegree 2010, regional case studies
[Step] Observation
  [Output] Italian and German printers converged on a small set of orthographic conventions within a generation
[Step] Counter-case
  [Output] French and Spanish standardisation followed central court / academy pressure decades later
The classic 'print caused standardisation' story holds only where commercial print markets were dense and crown-level language policy was absent. Where the crown intervened, standardisation predates print's market saturation, which complicates the causal direction.
